ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a circle, and point S is outside the circle at the lower right. From S, draw a horizontal ray to the left, tangent to the circle at R; from S, draw another ray to the upper left, passing through T and U on the circle, forming a secant. The figure marks the far intercepted arc RU as 179°, and the near intercepted arc RT as 71°. Reasoning: This is a tangent-secant angle formed by point S outside the circle. According to the external tangent-secant angle theorem, the measure of the exterior angle is equal to half the difference of the measures of the two intercepted arcs. Therefore m∠S = (179° - 71°) / 2 = 108° / 2 = 54°.
